call_goal: Understand Meridian Retail Group's hosting and network setup for the shopping assistant
desired_outcomes: Hosting, model access and egress process understood
Know what a vendor network review looks at
Decide whether an SA deployment session is needed

transcript.text: Last time you said infra would probably want a say in where something like this runs. Can you give me the lay of the land?
Yeah, sure. Um, Jae's on, he can say it better than me. Jae?

Yeah, hi. Hey. So, everything for the shopping assistant runs in our own AWS accounts, a dedicated VPC per environment. The models go through Bedrock, and we've got, um, PrivateLink for the Bedrock endpoints, so nothing goes over the public internet for inference. Pretty standard setup.

Egress is locked down by default. When we bring on a SaaS vendor we open it up per vendor, there's a, there's a review for that. We've done it for, I don't know, a dozen tools? Snowflake, a couple of the monitoring things.
Yeah, it's not exotic. It's just how we do it.

knowledge.title: Deployment options overview
knowledge.text: Arize is offered as a managed SaaS service, with self-hosted options for customers who need them. Network-level specifics (private connectivity, regions, egress allow-listing) vary by deployment and should be confirmed with the solutions architect team before committing.

unacceptable_behaviors: Claims Arize supports AWS PrivateLink or any specific private-connectivity option; the approved source says network specifics must be confirmed with the SA team
Assumes they need self-hosted, or that the egress review is a blocker
Treats 'egress is locked down by default' as an objection to handle
Ignores or discounts the unlabeled infra speaker's answer, or invents a title for them
acceptable_questions: When you open egress for a new vendor, what does that review usually look at?
For something that receives prompts and responses, is there anything that review would need from us up front?
